The Fed cuts, the market prices it in, and then immediately un-prices it. Now people are talking about term premium. Watching the screen tonight on /biz/, bond traders are losing their minds.

signal.rationale: OP screams yields ripping higher and term premium expanding = short duration trade

clips.text_en_b2: US treasuries are going absolutely haywire, with two-, ten-, and thirty-year yields all grinding higher simultaneously. Basis points keep ratcheting up, and term premium is creeping back into the picture even after the Fed's rate cut, which markets initially priced in and then immediately unpriced. Watching the bond action on /biz/ tonight, seasoned traders are throwing their hands up. Some joke that trading itself is the real tuition fee, and frankly, they're not entirely wrong. (79 words)
clips.text_en_c1: US Treasuries have gone completely berserk once again. Yields across the two-, ten-, and thirty-year tenors are marching upward in lockstep, with basis points ballooning beyond anything most newcomers ever anticipated. Whenever the Fed signals a cut, the market instantly prices it in, only to un-price the move moments later — a textbook case of whipsaw. The much-discussed term premium has now come roaring back, and bond traders over on /biz/ are watching their screens with a mixture of disbelief and despair.
clips.text_en_c2: The US Treasury complex is staging what can only be described as a synchronized rout across the entire curve, with two-, ten-, and thirty-year yields lurching upward in lockstep. Basis points are piling up so aggressively that the screen resembles a post-mortem in real time; novice retail inflows, seduced by the now-anachronistic conceit that duration is synonymous with safety, are being decapitated. After the Fed's cut, the market dutifully priced the dovish pivot, then proceeded to un-price it with almost theatrical indifference, as term premium reasserts itself with a vengeance. The refrain that trading is tuition has rarely felt less metaphorical, since the syllabus, the examination, and the burial have effectively collapsed into a single, brutal instant.

clips.text_en_b2: Doge's push to eliminate the penny is being torn apart on /biz/ as little more than a token gesture. Critics point out that the US Mint is essentially the only profitable branch of the entire government, so scrapping the coin amounts to cutting off your nose to spite your face. People are losing patience with these half-baked stunts and nothing-burger policies. One poster summed it up neatly, asking how anyone can take investment advice seriously from this crew. (83 words)
clips.text_en_c1: Doge's latest wheeze — eliminating the penny to manufacture a sense of accomplishment — is nothing short of performative vandalism. What the talking heads conveniently omit is that the US Mint remains the sole self-funding organ of the entire federal government, quietly turning a profit while every other department bleeds red ink. Scraping the one-cent coin would therefore amount to a textbook case of cutting off your nose to spite your face, eroding seigniorage revenue for the sake of a symbolic gesture. Meanwhile, the same administration that cannot even manage its own fiat urges ordinary citizens to pile into CFDs and leveraged futures, instruments that retail investors consistently underestimate.
clips.text_en_c2: Doge's campaign to abolish the penny, ostensibly framed as a fiscal rectification, is in fact a textbook exercise in cutting off one's nose to spite one's face. The US Mint remains, somewhat remarkably, the singular constituent of the federal apparatus that actually generates revenue, so culling its only meaningfully profitable denomination is not reform but symbolic vandalism masquerading as stewardship. The /biz/ consensus, articulated with weary contempt, treats the proposal as yet another hair-brained stunt, a nothing-burger of policy theatre calculated to flatter a particular constituency. That an administration simultaneously incapable of competently administering its currency circulation expects retail participation in CFDs and futures markets invites a contemptuous shrug. The whole episode epitomises a governance style that mistakes the optics of disruption for the substance of repair.

clips.text_zh: 今日返工睇一份 GI report，斜坡 factor of safety 又差唔多唔夠。地下排水管去水慢成龜速，雨水入晒土釘個面。Sum Ho 何生叫我諗下 load path 同 drainage 點解一齊壞。考牌都未溫完，仲要寫英文 memo，廢柴。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Today at work I read a ground investigation report on a slope site. The factor of safety was nearly too low. Underground drainage was too slow, so rainwater went straight into the soil nailing face. My boss Sum Ho asked me to explain why the load path and drainage failed at the same time. I still have to write the memo in English.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ Canada collapse thread used as prompt for civil life reflection
clips.text_en_b2: At the site today, I was reviewing a ground investigation report for a slope where the factor of safety was borderline inadequate. Underground drainage was dreadfully slow, so surface water had been seeping straight into the soil-nailing face. My supervisor Sum Ho wanted me to work out why the load path and the drainage system had failed in tandem, and to set it out in a formal English memo. I haven't even finished revising for my professional exam, and now this. (85 words)
clips.text_en_c1: Pulled up a ground investigation report first thing this morning and the figures were grim reading. The computed factor of safety for the slope was perilously close to the regulatory threshold, and the subsurface drainage network was discharging at an almost glacial pace. With nowhere else for the runoff to go, rainwater has been infiltrating the exposed soil-nailing face, undermining the very mechanism meant to retain it. My supervising engineer, Sum Ho, has tasked me with articulating precisely why the load path and the hydraulic regime appear to be failing in concert rather than isolation.
clips.text_en_c2: This morning at the site office I was obliged to wade through a ground investigation report whose findings bordered on the alarming: the assessed factor of safety for the slope under review had degraded to the very threshold of acceptability, rendering the margin between stability and catastrophic failure almost vanishingly thin. Compounding matters, the subsurface drainage network was discharging at a pace so glacial that stormwater had effectively migrated into the soil-nailing face, saturating it precisely where tensile capacity is most critical. My principal, Mr Ho, requested a written explication of how the load path and the drainage regime had contrived to fail in concert, a question whose answer demands more epistemic humility than my professional formation has yet equipped me to supply.

clips.text_en_b2: Burning the midnight oil on FE prep tonight, and beam-column load paths are still giving me absolute nightmares. RC design requires me to justify the chosen method and back it up with proper checks, while steel design throws lateral-torsional buckling into the mix. clips.text_en_c1: Spent the entire evening grinding through FE revision, and the section on beam-column load paths once again proved to be my nemesis. The reinforced-concrete portion demands not only a defensible choice of design method but also a rigorous justification for why that particular approach was selected over the alternatives. The steel segment, meanwhile, obliges me to verify lateral-torsional buckling by hand — a calculation that is every bit as tedious as it sounds. On top of all this academic torment, Tommy has requested that I submit a condition survey by tomorrow morning and append a written explanation of the governing failure mode.
clips.text_en_c2: Yet another evening spent wrestling with FE examination material, and once again the choreography of beam-column load paths has reduced me to a state of quiet despair. Reinforced concrete design demands not merely the application of a methodology but a forensic justification for its selection, alongside the requisite verification checks that distinguish competent practice from mere box-ticking; steel design, for its part, insists upon a meticulous appraisal of lateral-torsional buckling, that most insidious of failure modes which punishes even minor lapses in restraint detailing. My supervising engineer, Tommy, has commissioned a condition survey for tomorrow's submission, accompanied by a written exegesis of the prevailing failure mechanism.

clips.text_en_c1: The doomers over on /pol/ are in full apocalyptic flourish tonight, and for once the underlying fundamentals almost warrant the hysteria. Russia, historically one of the world's foremost diesel exporters, has steadily throttled its outbound shipments while domestic refineries keep suffering what look like suspiciously convenient operational setbacks. Should the United States — the single largest diesel exporter on the planet — go offline in tandem, the cascading consequences would be severe and immediate. The so-called Oil Arabia would, in effect, be reduced to little more than Sand Arabia, with precious hydrocarbons actually leaving the region.
clips.text_en_c2: The /pol/ discourse this evening has escalated into something approaching apocalyptic prognostication, with posters contending that the global diesel supply architecture is approaching a precipitous inflection point. Russia's erstwhile pre-eminence as a distillate exporter has eroded under the cumulative attrition of refinery strikes, while the United States, the world's largest residual supplier, now teeters on the brink of analogous disruption. The resultant vacuum would propagate, the thread insists, across every principal importing bloc: India, China, the broader Asian constellation, the African continent, and Australia would all confront shortages of a commodity upon which freight, agriculture, and power generation remain acutely dependent.

clips.text_en_c2: The nostalgia-industrial complex of /a/ has, with admirable punctuality, inaugurated another of its beloved retro-anime retrospectives, this iteration focusing upon the somewhat underappreciated noughties as a locus of rediscovery. Contributors have already nominated a fairly canonical slate including Hellsing, Wolf's Rain, Bleach, and Azumanga Daioh, each title functioning as a kind of generational shibboleth for viewers whose formative consumption occurred during that peculiarly fertile interregnum between the second golden age of OVAs and the streaming-era monoculture. Seasonal offerings, while ostensibly current and algorithmically optimised, evidently lack the affective density that older productions accumulate through sheer temporal accretion.
